ui.update: This code needs a newer version of the app.
ui.expired: This code has expired. Get a new one.
ui.unreachable: This service can't be reached from your wallet.
ui.pass-on: No message: the text goes to the consumer's other handlers, unchanged.

config.notes: Spec section 7 defines how to use this file. input is the scanned, opened or pasted text; channel is scan, deeplink or paste and never changes a core result. An accept lists via (url), from, id, exp (or null), flow (the config label, or null when there is no hint), task (uri, major, minor, or null) and ignored (fragment.<name> for each unknown name that begins with an underscore, in document order). Flows match by the whole URI without its version segment. A draft flow accepts only the listed MINORs; a stable flow accepts any MINOR of a listed MAJOR. A trigger is expired when exp + skew <= now. The host example.com and the prefix https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/flow/ are fixtures and proposals: the prefix is not registered; tasks.example.org, example-stable and the alias scheme examplewallet are test-only. ui follows the reason as in spec section 3. selectionVectors take a DID document and test spec section 5 rule 5 only; the consumer's preference order there is a fixture. legacyVectors test the annex's legacy reader (annex F), not the core, under config.legacy.

selection.unmappedTypes: any other service type, including TSPTransport (reserved, not a verified service type), is not a candidate

outcomes.select: binding and endpoint taken from the DID document; nothing is sent by this step
outcomes.no-common-transport: no candidate: nothing is sent; ui unreachable
outcomes.reject: nothing is sent; reason did-document-unverified; ui invalid

selection.notes: The preference order is a test fixture, not any wallet's order. DIDComm accept and the order of services of different types do not choose a binding; among candidates of one type the first in document order wins. A service whose endpoint fails the host rules or is not https is not a candidate.

ui.scan-only: Scan the code on the website's screen.

legacy.notes: Annex F. The legacy reader runs only on text the core passes on (not-ours). It reports ignored members as legacy.<key> in document order and adds callbackUrl to an accept.

vectors.note: a ? inside the fragment is not a separator: the name is x?_from, which is not reserved, so _from is missing
the previous query container: the reserved names in the query are not read
reserved names in the query are never read, even beside a fragment trigger
a tracker appends to the query, which is not read
